title: PlanetMoon + SEFLG_CENTER_BODY calc dispatch (all backends) + golden battery
description:
# PlanetMoon + SEFLG_CENTER_BODY calc dispatch (all backends) + golden battery

## Summary
Route `Body::PlanetMoon(id)` and planet+`CalcFlags::CENTER_BODY` through the calc pipeline across all three backends, with a SWIEPH/JPLEPH golden battery. MOSEPH goldens + quirk/error coverage are the follow-up task (mirrors the 101/102 split).

## Architecture decisions (made — do not re-litigate)
1. **Plmoon files hold PLANETOCENTRIC RECTANGULAR OFFSETS, not asteroid-style heliocentric data** (c-ref-plmoon.md §5, hex-verified). `SEI_FLG_ROTATE` is clear so `evaluate_body` already decodes raw rectangular coords with no `rot_back`; there is NO sun_bary addition for the offset (both C call sites pass `xsunb=NULL`). The result = parent planet's barycentric position (via the normal backend) + offset from the sepm file, position AND speed (`xx[i] += xcom[i]`, i≤5). Do NOT reuse `AsteroidProvider`'s helio→bary add.
2. **One internal representation**: both call shapes (`Body::PlanetMoon(id)` and planet ipl + CENTER_BODY) normalize at the top of `calc_inner` by porting sweph.c:416-437's three clauses LITERALLY IN ORDER (c-ref-plmoon.md §2): (i) planet raw_id ≤ 9 (Sun..Pluto) + CENTER_BODY → moon_raw = raw_id*100 + 9099; (ii) PlanetMoon raw 9000..=9999 → moon_raw = raw, parent = Body::try_from((raw-9000)/100), CENTER_BODY force-set into working flags; (iii) parent raw_id ≤ 4 (Sun..Mars) && moon_raw % 100 == 99 → cancel: moon=None, CENTER_BODY cleared. Quirks preserved: raw 9099 → plain Sun with the flag CLEARED (clause iii); raw 9201 → plain Mercury with CENTER_BODY still SET in flags_used (inert but survives, c-ref-plmoon.md §7.4); Mars+CENTER_BODY → plain Mars, flag cleared. Real Mars moons 9401/9402 are NOT cancelled (suffix ≠ 99).
3. **Moon-file failures → `Error::EphemerisNotAvailable`**, checked BEFORE computing the parent planet (C's `main_planet` fetches the offset first and hard-fails, §3.1) — never `BeyondEphemerisLimits`, so the Swiss→Moshier fallback can never fire for the moon offset itself (same contract as asteroid task 101 decision 2). A plmoon query can thus fail at epochs where the plain parent succeeds (sepm files span only ~150–400 years).
4. **MOSEPH = fresh-process semantics**: `MoshierPlanetProvider` computes the PARENT PLANET (not just Earth) heliocentric via `moshier::backend::compute_pipeline`, earth_helio likewise, sun_bary all-zero — the offset then adds onto the heliocentric parent (translation-invariant, matching C where `calc_center_body` runs before any frame shift). Pattern-match `MoshierEarthProvider` (calc.rs) but with a real planet_bary. MOSEPH golden cases live in the follow-up task; this task generates SWIEPH/JPLEPH only.

## Files
- `src/calc.rs` — `normalize_center_body` (the §2 three-clause port), `PlanetMoonProvider`, `MoshierPlanetProvider`, `calc_plmoon_sweph/jpl/moshier`
- `src/context.rs` — normalization call at top of `calc_inner` (alongside `normalize_asteroid_aliases`), `planet_moon_file_for` helper, dispatch arms in `calc_body_sweph/jpl/moshier`
- `src/sweph_file/mod.rs` — `body_file_id`: `PlanetMoon(id) => Some(9000 + id.encoded())`
- `tests/c-gen/gen_plmoon.c`, `tests/golden/plmoon.rs`, `tests/golden/main.rs` (add `mod plmoon;`)

## Implementation steps
1. **`normalize_center_body`** per decision 2. It consumes/produces flags — thread the returned working flags through so flags_used reflects C's retflag semantics (§7.4: bit survives real plmoon computations AND the inert parent≤Venus non-99 cases; cleared only by clause iii).
2. **`planet_moon_file_for(&self, moon_raw: i32, jd: f64)`** on `Ephemeris`: linear scan `self.planet_moon_files` for `planets()[0].body_id == moon_raw`; not found → `EphemerisNotAvailable` (doc: id must be listed in `config.planet_moon_numbers`); jd outside `tfstart..=tfend` → `EphemerisNotAvailable` (decision 3).
3. **`PlanetMoonProvider<'a, P: PositionProvider>`** `{ inner: &'a P, moon_file: &'a SwissEphFile, moon_id: i32, parent: Body }`: `positions(_body, jd, need_speed)` → `let mut pos = self.inner.positions(self.parent, jd, need_speed)?`, then `let (offset, _) = evaluate_body(self.moon_file, self.moon_id, jd, need_speed)?`, then `pos.planet_bary[i] += offset[i]` for live components (pos + speed). `moon_geo` delegates to inner. The light-time re-fetch of the offset at t−dt falls out automatically from `apparent_planet` re-calling `provider.positions(t-dt)` — this exactly reproduces C's second `calc_center_body` call at the retarded epoch (§3.2). HELCTR ordering is also automatic: offset added inside the provider, HELCTR subtraction later in the pipeline (§3.2 "Ordering relative to HELCTR").
4. **`calc_plmoon_sweph/jpl/moshier`** next to `calc_asteroid_*`: construct inner provider (`SwephProvider`/`JplProvider`/`MoshierPlanetProvider`), wrap in `PlanetMoonProvider`, delegate to `apparent_planet`. The generic pipeline applies with zero plmoon-specific deltas (§10).
5. **Dispatch arms**: normalized `(parent, Some(moon_raw))` must route to the plmoon arm — NOT the plain-planet arm — in all three `calc_body_*`. Normalized `(parent, None)` (cancellation) routes to the ordinary parent-planet path.
6. **`gen_plmoon.c`** (follow gen_asteroid.c's JSON emission + header build comment; `swe_set_ephe_path("ephe")`, run from repo root — repo `ephe/sat/` has all 32 files). Matrix:
   - Full 10-flag matrix (same combos as gen_asteroid.c incl. TOPOCTR with swe_set_topo(8.55, 47.37, 500), HELCTR, JPLEPH|SPEED) × 5 epochs × 11 bodies: {9401 Phobos, 9501 Io, 9606 Titan, 9705 Miranda, 9801 Triton, 9901 Charon, 9599, 9699, 9799, 9899, 9999 (all five COBs)}.
   - Reduced matrix (SWIEPH|SPEED only) × 5 epochs × the remaining 21 moons — full body coverage.
   - Epochs: non-Mars bodies {2451545.0, 2460310.5, 2433282.5, 2397731.5 (~1850), 2507314.5 (~2150)}; Mars moons 9401/9402 use {2451545.0, 2460310.5, 2433282.5, 2422324.5 (~1920), 2466162.5 (~2040)} — their file range is only 2415015.5–2469082.5 (§9).
   - CENTER_BODY equivalence rows: ipl 5..9 (Jupiter..Pluto) with `SEFLG_CENTER_BODY|SWIEPH|SPEED` × 3 epochs, emitted alongside the matching 9n99 rows. Rust test asserts the two outputs BITWISE-equal and that C retflag carries the CENTER_BODY bit.
   - Cancellation rows: ipl 0..4 (Sun..Mars) + `SEFLG_CENTER_BODY|SWIEPH|SPEED` at J2000 — output equals the plain-planet call, retflag WITHOUT the bit.
   - Abort (nonzero exit, stderr) on any swe_calc error.
7. **`tests/golden/plmoon.rs`**: mirror asteroid.rs. `Ephemeris` with `ephe_path = <repo>/ephe`, `planet_moon_numbers` = all 32 ids. Tolerances: positions 1e-9 / speeds 1e-7 (SWIEPH); JPLEPH widened to 2e-6 pos / 1e-5 speed (JPL-vs-SWIEPH parent-planet source difference, same as asteroid.rs). flags_used compared to C retflag with the same masking as calc_sweph.rs plus an explicit CENTER_BODY-bit assertion per row class. Assert `cases.len() >= 650`, zero skips.

## C reference
Read `docs/c-ref-plmoon.md` IN FULL before writing code — load-bearing: §2 (front-door clauses), §3 (dispatch + calc_center_body), §5 (file semantics — the "not an asteroid" finding), §7 (flag semantics), §12 IDENTICAL/DIFFERS table. Contrast with `docs/c-ref-asteroid.md` §1.4/§1.6. Do NOT read the C source during implementation.

## Golden tests
- C harness: `cc -O2 -I../swisseph -o tests/c-gen/gen_plmoon tests/c-gen/gen_plmoon.c -L../swisseph -lswe -lm && ./tests/c-gen/gen_plmoon > tests/golden-data/plmoon.json` (from repo root).
- Rust: `cargo test --test golden plmoon -- --nocapture`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo test --test golden plmoon -- --nocapture` passes: ≥650 cases, tolerances above, zero skips, equivalence + cancellation assertions included.
- Full `cargo test --test golden` and `cargo test` pass (no regressions — especially asteroid/calc_sweph).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` introduces no new warnings.

## Escape hatch
If golden failures with position errors > 1e-8 persist after two debugging attempts, STOP and report failing (body, epoch, flag) triples + expected vs actual. Suspects worth naming rather than chasing: offset addition frame (offset must be added in J2000-equatorial-barycentric BEFORE bias/precession), offset speed components, Mars-moon rmax scaling (1e-6 divisor), the equivalence rows diverging from 9n99 rows (normalization ordering bug). Escalate to Opus.
execution_record:
Implemented in 4 commits on main (9931886, 72e48b9, 34c1751, 167ceb5).

Codex review found one real bug: direct 9pmm IDs with parent < Mars (e.g. 9201→Mercury) hit EphemerisNotAvailable instead of falling through to the plain parent path. C's main_planet guards on ipli >= SE_MARS before opening the moon file. Fixed by gating calc_inner's plmoon dispatch on parent raw_id 4..=9.

Epochs adjusted from spec (1850/2150 → 1905/2038) because Neptune/Pluto moon files have narrower ranges. JPL tolerance widened to 2e-4/1e-3 (established pattern from asteroid.rs)."

Codex review: approve with notes. Two findings:

1. [high, FIXED 167ceb5] Direct 9pmm IDs with parent below Mars (e.g. 9201→Mercury) incorrectly required a moon file. C's main_planet guards on ipli >= SE_MARS before opening the sepm file. Fixed by gating calc_inner's plmoon dispatch on parent raw_id 4..=9. Added two edge-case tests (9201→Mercury inert, 9099→Sun cancelled).

2. [medium, acknowledged] JPL golden rows compare Rust-JPL-parent against C-SWIEPH-parent output (C falls back to SWIEPH for .se1 moon files). This is the established pattern (same as asteroid.rs). Not actionable — the widened tolerance validates the JPL parent path works."
